subject: Hosted API evaluation — sandbox access & traffic envelope
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@pocketpay.com>
Cc: Anjali Rao <anjali.rao@pocketpay.com>
Date: Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 3:12 PM -0700
Subject: Hosted API evaluation — next steps and quickstart access

Hi Liam / Anjali —

Thanks for the demo earlier today — great conversation and appreciate the clarity on the fraud-prevention use case. Quick recap and the asks I promised: —

1) Deployment preference: you mentioned wanting to start on Hosted API to iterate quickly and then evaluate Dedicated if throughput grows. Please confirm that's still the plan.

2) Traffic envelope: rough QPS, average tokens per call, payload size, and peak concurrency. If you can drop a CSV with a day-of-week sample that helps.

3) Quickstart sandbox: we'll provision a hosted sandbox with two endpoints ("ingest" and "scoring") and a pre-configured rate limit of 50 req/s by default for the trial. If you'd like higher initial limits we can provision an increase for the demo window.

4) SLO/latency targets: you said <250ms P95 for scoring — confirm target and acceptable fallback behavior (queueing vs rate-limit-reject).

5) Security/compliance: we'll need your list of egress regions and any IP allowlist entries for the sandbox. For production Private/VPC conversations we can loop security.

Next steps I propose:
- You send the traffic envelope CSV and confirm the latency SLO and deployment preference.
- I'll loop in Aditya (SE) to stand up the sandbox and Monica (CS) for onboarding and success plan.

Attaching a short quickstart checklist and a sample traffic template to make the CSV quick.

Thanks —

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[karthik@redwood.ai] [555-650-1128]
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf, traffic-envelope-sample.csv

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@pocketpay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anjali Rao <anjali.rao@pocketpay.com>
Date: Mon, Apr 5, 2027 at 9:03 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation — next steps and quickstart access

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirmations and answers below:

- Deployment preference: yes, start with Hosted API for the pilot (we want the faster onboarding path) and we will evaluate Dedicated if traffic economics make sense in Q3.

- Traffic envelope: attached is a quick sample (day-of-week rows) with estimated QPS and avg tokens. Baseline expected: 30 req/s average, 120 req/s peak for a short 2-hour window. Avg tokens per call ~180 (scoring), ingest calls are smaller ~40 tokens. Payloads for scoring are JSON blobs ~2–3 KB.

- Latency SLO: target is P95 < 250ms for scoring. If we hit a temporary spike, we prefer graceful degradation (reject excess with 429 rather than queueing) so frontend can show a degraded UX.

- Security: sandbox egress from us-west-2 only; we'll provide static IP ranges for our NATs next day.

Please go ahead and provision the sandbox with endpoints "/v1/ingest" and "/v1/scoring". For the trial window (next 7 days) bump rate limits to 150 req/s on scoring so we can run peak tests.

Appreciate it —

Liam O'Connor
Head of Engineering | PocketPay
liam@pocketpay.com

Attachment: pocketpay-traffic-envelope-sample.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam@pocketpay.com>, Anjali Rao <anjali.rao@pocketpay.com>
Date: Mon, Apr 5, 2027 at 11:28 AM -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API evaluation — next steps and quickstart access

Folks — forwarding PocketPay's answers and sample CSV. TL;DR: they want Hosted sandbox, two endpoints (/v1/ingest, /v1/scoring), baseline 30 req/s, peak 120 req/s (requesting we raise to 150 req/s for a 7-day peak test), avg scoring tokens ~180, scoring P95 target <250ms, prefer 429 on overload.

Action items: 
- Aditya: can you provision the sandbox in us-west-2 and map endpoints to the trial endpoints? Please set scoring limit to 150 req/s for the 7-day window and document the exact per-endpoint quotas in the invite. Include a short snippet for client retry/backoff guidance.
- Monica: please prepare the onboarding playbook, set up the success check-in cadence (Day 1 smoke, Day 3 peak test, Day 7 review), and include an ops contact for out-of-hours. Also capture any cost expectations for their peak tests.

Liam — I'll confirm when access is ready.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, Apr 6, 2027 at 11:05 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation — sandbox provisioned + credentials

Hi all —

Sandbox is live in us-west-2. Summary of provisioning: 

- Endpoints created: /v1/ingest (api-key scoped to ingest), /v1/scoring (api-key scoped to scoring).
- Scoring rate limit: 150 req/s for 7 days (window expires 2027-04-13 23:59:59 UTC). Baseline default for scoring after expiry will be 50 req/s.
- Ingest rate limit: 100 req/s.
- Tokens: we instrumented token-logging for the trial; you will see token counts in the usage dashboard.
- Latency: endpoints routed to an optimized instance profile; expected P95 under typical load ~120–180ms.

Credentials and docs: attached sandbox-invite-credentials.txt (API keys + a small curl example), and I've linked the quickstart checklist for onboarding.

Retries/backoff recommendation: 429 => exponential backoff (Jittered) starting at 200ms, max backoff 5s. We will provide a client snippet in Node and Python in the shared Drive folder.

Monica — I left a note in the onboarding doc where you can drop the check-in schedule and billing snapshot.

Liam — confirm you received the credentials and we can schedule the Day 1 smoke check tomorrow morning.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai

Attachments: sandbox-invite-credentials.txt, redwood-hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf
